title: WebKit's Open-Sourcing and the Blink Fork (2005, 2013)
explainer: Apple open-sourced WebKit, itself originally forked from KDE's KHTML engine, in June 2005, inviting outside contribution to a shared browser engine. By 2013, the changes Google needed for Chrome's multi-process architecture had diverged so far from that shared codebase that Google forked it into Blink rather than continuing to push everything upstream. The episode is a concrete illustration of the real tension in upstream contribution: how long do you keep merging into a shared project before forking becomes the practical choice?

title: io.js: A Fork Born From a Governance Dispute (2014)
explainer: In December 2014, developer Fedor Indutny forked Node.js into io.js, not over a technical disagreement but because he wanted more open governance and faster adoption of new V8 engine releases than Joyent's stewardship allowed at the time. The fork gained enough traction that the Node.js Foundation formed in February 2015 and merged the two codebases back together as Node.js v4.0 that September, showing how a credible fork can act as upstream leverage rather than a permanent split.
